formal_record.question:
A piece of paper numbered 1 to 36 is folded in half twice, as shown.
A hole is then punched through all four layers at the position shown in the right-hand diagram. Which four numbers are pierced?
Choices:
A:$8,11,26,29$
B:$14,16,21,23$
C:$14,17,20,23$
D:$15,16,21,22$
E:$15,17,20,22$

mechanism: The existing punched-hole boundary is red, paired with the four existing boundaries of originalcell15. This is a concrete false hole-to-cell correspondence, encouraging the columnshift that selects the central pair3/4 rather than true columns2/5. It predicts the fourfold orbit15,16,21,22 (D), while fold arrows and original numbers remain legible.
mathematical_solution: Number r,c is6(r-1)+c with top rowr1. Horizontal fold pairs rowsr and7-r; subsequent vertical fold pairs columnsc and7-c. The hole at final topmiddle square corresponds to original rows3,4 and cols2,5, giving14,17,20,23 uniquely optionC. The marked cell15 has rows3,4 and cols3,4 orbit15,16,21,22, a different orbit (D). Outline recoloring neither moves the punch nor makes cell15 pierced as a condition.
